question: Do the 220 LiteInst rows in compat-envelope/scorecard.csv reproduce when LiteInst is driven through the EXPANSION RUNNER (expansion-dag.rs + safe-ci-dag-runner) instead of a bare `hermit run` CLI, as the predecessor's lead predicted?
verdict: NO. The expansion runner cannot have produced those rows, and LiteInst does not activate in ANY invocation context on this host.

host.note: This is the SAME host recorded in the metadata.json of both producers of the 220 rows, so 'host-specific to some other box' is refuted, not merely untested.

toolchain.runtime_env: LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/newton/.local/hermit-deps/lu/usr/lib64 (required: every hermit build here has an unresolved libunwind-x86_64.so.8; NOT recorded by any producer)

binaries_under_test.reverie_sha_source: derived from Cargo.lock of the pinned tree at 464cbd9f (rrnewton/reverie git rev)
binaries_under_test.why: This is EXACTLY the (hermit, reverie) pair recorded on all 220 LiteInst rows of compat-envelope/scorecard.csv. Binary provenance is SELF-ATTESTED by `hermit --version`, not assumed from a mtime.
A clean, recent SHA at which 28 e2e cells actually ENABLE liteinst, so the expansion runner can reach hermit at all. Used read-only; no build was performed in any slot.

binaries_under_test.caveat: NOT REPRODUCIBLE FROM THIS RECORD: the tree was dirty, and another agent rebuilt the primary during this session (it now self-reports gf89c69766371-dirty). Recorded as a third invariance datapoint only; the two clean-SHA probes above are the load-bearing ones.

source_trees.method: read-only `git clone --shared --no-checkout` + detached checkout under scratch/ so that ROOT_DIR's `git rev-parse HEAD` matches the binary's self-reported SHA and `git status --porcelain` is empty. No worktree was created, no slot HEAD was moved, no build was run in any slot.

commands: ci/test_harness.sh run --lane portable --category c-programs --test c-programs/acct-refusal-probe --mode verify --backend liteinst --include-manual
seed: n/a (no randomised input; chaos mode was not exercised)

iterations.note: Single iteration per cell, as in the prior run. Justified here because the observed failure is deterministic and total (0/28 LiteInst cells reached the guest; 28/28 ptrace reference cells passed in the SAME context), not marginal - a repeat-count study would only re-measure a 0%/100% split. It is NOT justified for any future run that reports a partial LiteInst pass rate.

limitations: ONE HOST (devbig014). Unlike the prior run this is not merely 'untested elsewhere' - it is the same host both producers recorded, which is what makes the non-reproduction load-bearing rather than environmental.

Arm D used 28 of the 1087 cells expansion-dag.rs emits for those buckets: exactly the cells whose manifest ENABLES liteinst at 52d56e5c. The other 1059 are manifest-disabled and are refused by the cell runner (same mechanism as arm C).

3 of those 28 came from expansion-dag.rs's own enumeration; 25 had to be synthesised into the DAG by hand because of the enumeration hole documented in README finding 5. The synthesised steps reuse expansion-dag.rs's OWN generated run-expansion-cell.sh helper and the identical cmd template, so the execution context is the runner's, not mine.

Arm D raised the per-step budgets over expansion-dag.rs's defaults (timeout 600, cpu_timeout 180) to defeat the 10 s CPU cap of README finding 6. LiteInst's verdict is unaffected - it fails in ~150 ms - but the ptrace reference could not complete under the stock budget.
I did NOT root-cause the handshake failure. That is ai_docs/liteinst-preload-handshake-root-cause-narrowed_20260806.md's open work; this experiment only adds the cross-build invariance datapoint.

I did not check whether the 136 recorded passes were genuine at the time they were recorded (e.g. recorded from a fallback path). This experiment shows only that they cannot be reproduced from what was recorded.
